Done. Committed on `feat/progress-and-joinall` as `22f2f77`.

## Results

**D1 — the defect reproduces.** Fitted exponent **2.256** (R²=0.9991) on 143 KB pieces: 1.20 / 34.7 / 150.1 / 667.9 ms at 24/99/198/396. The brief's 2.028 and its absolute times land in the same place.

**D2 — the fix.**
```hoon
++  join-all
  |=  parts=(list octs)
  ^-  octs
  :-  (roll parts |=([piece=octs total=@ud] (add p.piece total)))
  (can 3 parts)
```
`(list octs)` nests under `(list [p=step q=@])` directly — no `turn`. `can` applies the same `end`/`lsh` per piece that `join` did, so the three edge cases hold by construction: `~` → `[0 0]`, `p=0` contributes nothing (even with junk in `q`), and `p > (met 3 q)` still advances the full `p`. That last one is what keeps tar padding and the 20-byte OID field in `tree-record` aligned.

**D3 — all 32 sites audited**, listed per-file in the report. Two groups mattered: `git-archive.hoon` (fixed-width tar fields, the `[1.024 0]` terminator, the `padded` octs from `file-entry`) and the `[0 0]` sentinels in `handle-upload-pack` at `urgit.hoon:7918/7921/7964/7970`. Neither depends on the fold shape. `git-github.hoon`'s three sites were read but not exercised live.

**D4 — byte-identical**, verified old→new→old→new with the running source scried between flips:
- wire `git-upload-pack` response `cmp`-identical, pack SHA-1 `29a0e12004afe9342195d8af8bd25871292c7687`
- real 1.2 MB repository tar `cmp`-identical
- all 18 vectors unchanged
- `git fsck --full` clean on four clones (v0, v2, shallow, unshallowed), one object set across all four

**D5 — exponent now 1.129**, and **1.008** between 198 and 396 pieces; the residual sits entirely in the 24-piece segment where a ~0.1 ms fixed cost dominates. 0.144 / 0.873 / 1.691 / 3.400 ms.

**Erpit scale is measured, not projected** — a 9,016-object / 207 MB pack runs, so I ran it: `encode-pack` **62.198 s → 1.081 s**, identical pack `mug`. It is erpit's *shape*, not erpit's repository, and the report says so.

Two things to flag:

- **The fence held but was worth checking.** Three instruments at widening scope give 196× / 57.6× / 2.9×. The last is `curl` wall time from outside the ship. The ratios shrinking as scope widens is the expected signature; had the outer one not moved, the build path would have been the suspect.
- **After the fix, `join-all` is no longer the top term in `git-upload-pack`.** `encode-pack` is ~0.16 s of a ~0.61 s round trip on that repository; the other ~0.45 s is unattributed. That is in the report's "could not measure" section along with the v2 push returning HTTP 400 — which reproduces on unmodified code and is not from this change.
